Today's release of the sixth beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate Bridge includes a brand new Golden Gate Bridge dynamic wallpaper, bringing the total number of dynamic wallpapers to five. All can be downloaded below.

The macOS 27 Golden Gate Bridge wallpaper gallery continues to expand

When Apple unveiled macOS 27 Golden Gate Bridge at WWDC26, it showcased the same system wallpaper across all its operating systems, featuring a stylized number "27" as its theme.

However, after several developer betas, Apple began adding dynamic screensavers that double as wallpapers, which include stunning slow-motion footage looking down on San Francisco's iconic Golden Gate Bridge.

When the Mac is unlocked, the screensaver gradually slows to a stop, and after each pause it leaves behind a fresh and slightly different wallpaper.

Although the dynamic effects are handled by macOS, what follows is a gallery of still frames from the four videos, along with light and dark versions of the universal stylized "27" wallpaper.

Be sure to click on the images and save the full resolution versions. To set one as your background, go to System Settings > Wallpaper, scroll down to Your Photos, click the Add Photo button, then do any of the following:

Add a photo from your Photos library: Click Choose from Photos, then select a photo. Add an image file: Click Choose File, select the file and click Open. You can also drag an image from your desktop or a folder onto a thumbnail at the top of the wallpaper settings. Add a folder from Finder: Click Choose Folder, select the folder and click Open. Add an album or folder from the Photos app: Select an album or folder under Collections.

According to Apple, "you can also choose a custom wallpaper without opening wallpaper settings":

Use a photo from your Photos library: Go to the Photos app, select a photo, click the share button in the Photos toolbar, then click Set as Wallpaper. Use an image found online: Control-click the image in a Safari window, then choose Use Image as Desktop Wallpaper. Use an image stored on your Mac: Click the Finder icon in the Dock to open a Finder window. Control-click the image file, then click Set as Desktop Picture.

To learn more about how to set a custom wallpaper in macOS, please visit this link.

Do you have a favorite? Let us know in the comments section.
